item.title: Pagkakaisa — Mon Aug 17, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Exhibition featuring OCAD U alums at Toronto City Hall as part of Mabuhay Philippines Festival.
In 1975, Filipino psychologist Virgilio G. Enriquez introduced the concept of Kapwa , a framework based on the idea of a “shared identity,” describing the bond between Filipino individuals and their communities. Pagkakaisa (pronounced pag-ka-ka-ee-sa ) is the Tagalog term for collective unity. Drawing from isa , meaning “one,” the title recognizes community as fundamental to Filipino culture, continuing within diasporic communities. Presented as part of the 2026 Mabuhay Festival, Pagkakaisa (Aug. 17 to 20) unites alums from OCAD University and the Philippine Artists Group of Canada, showcasing contemporary work by Filipino-Canadian artists. Curated by OCAD U graduates Jewel and Kristina Pavao. Featured artists (and OCAD U alums) are: John Calara Mare Garcia Jillian Hernandez (jfh) Azia Jonelle R.J. item.title: Caves, Cliffs, and Crevices: The Duncan Caves Loop — Sat Sep 12, 7:30 AM
item.description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club **Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/duncan-caves)**
**Join us as we head to the Duncan escarpment to explore some incredible ‘crevice’ or ‘fracture’ caves, created over thousands of years through a mixture of glacial movement, extreme temperatures and the raw force of gravity.**
We start the hike through open farmland and meadow before the ground tilts up and we climb onto the escarpment itself. From there, most of the day is spent walking along the escarpment and through the forest that grows right up to the cliff edge and spill over its exposed rock.
We will then descend into the caves, with some being over 30 metres deep. You will be scrambling in some places, working your way down and through one of the more unique pieces of trail anywhere in Ontario.
